evidence.text: No Reports Does a viral video show a life-threatening attack on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu one day after the Oct. 27, 2026, election? No, that's not true: The low quality of the video obscured that it showed a different politician giving a speech in a different country in 2013. It was Ahmed Dogan attacked in Bulgaria. The claim appeared in a post (archived here ) by @AsifAli_Haider on Oct. 28, 2026. It opened: Breaking 🚨 A very dangerous attack on Netanyahu in Tel Aviv it appears he has sustained severe injuries, and an aircraft is being dispatched to transport him to the United States. This is clearly evident from the footage. Don't remove my video X Twitter This is what a screenshot of the video looked like on X at the time of writing: (Image source: post by @AsifAli_Haide

Don't remove my video X Twitter This is what a screenshot of the video looked like on X at the time of writing: (Image source: post by @AsifAli_Haider on X.) Figure caption, The gunman did not succeed in making a shot A man put a gas pistol to the head of the leader of Bulgaria's ethnic Turkish party during a televised conference. Ahmed Dogan, leader of the Movement for Rights and Freedoms (MRF) was unharmed and the unidentified man was wrestled to the ground by security guards. The incident happened on Saturday at a party congress in the capital Sofia. Interior Minister Tsvetan Tsvetanov said the attacker, himself an ethnic Turk, tried to fire two shots but "most likely the gun misfired". Early reports suggested the weapon was a gun, but it was later confirmed to be a gas pistol - a non-lethal weapon used largely for self-defence which does not fire bullets but which can cause serious injuries if fired from close range. Mr Tsetanov also said t

orts suggested the weapon was a gun, but it was later confirmed to be a gas pistol - a non-lethal weapon used largely for self-defence which does not fire bullets but which can cause serious injuries if fired from close range. Mr Tsetanov also said the assailant had a criminal record for drugs possession, robberies and hooliganism. Police arrested the attacker, a 25-year-old from the Black Sea town of Burgas, who was also carrying two knives. The liberal MRF party represents ethnic Turks and other Muslims, who make up about 12% of Bulgaria's population of about seven million. Mr Dogan, 58, has led the party for almost 25 years. He returned to the party conference a few hours after the attack and was given a standing ovation. President Rosen Plevneliev said in a statement: "Bulgarian societ

pulation of about seven million. Mr Dogan, 58, has led the party for almost 25 years. He returned to the party conference a few hours after the attack and was given a standing ovation. President Rosen Plevneliev said in a statement: "Bulgarian society is traditionally known for its tolerance, mutual acceptance and respect between different ethnic groups and religions. "Such an act is unacceptable in a democratic state." Attacks on politicians are rare in Bulgaria, but in 1996, former Prime Minister Andrei Lukanov was found shot dead near his home in Sofia. evidence.text: Judgment in relation to the appeals was handed down on Friday 30 October at 10am. The two appeals were an appeal by Erin Patterson for the Court of Appeal to review and overturn the findings of guilt from the trial (an appeal against conviction), and an appeal by the DPP against the sentence imposed. The Court of Appeal livestreamed the appeal decisions. Following a jury trial which ran from April to July last year, Ms Patterson was found guilty of murdering her parents-in-law Don and Gail Patterson and her aunt-in-law Heather Wilkinson. She was also found guilty of the attempted murder of her uncle-in-law Ian Wilkinson.
